issues.title: Thread safety violation calling @MainActor completion handler from background thread
issues.description: In the handleServerTrust method, when SSL/TLS certificate validation fails (guard else clause), the @MainActor-isolated completionHandler is called directly from the background dispatchQueue without using ensureMainThread wrapper. This violates Swift Concurrency's actor isolation and can cause runtime crashes or data races. The success path correctly wraps the completion call in ensureMainThread, but the failure path at line 1343 does not, creating inconsistent thread safety behavior.

issues.title: ensureMainThread generic function loses return value when dispatched asynchronously
issues.description: The generic ensureMainThread<T> function was modified to return T? but has a critical flaw: when not on the main thread, it dispatches the work asynchronously to main queue and immediately returns nil, discarding the actual computation result. This breaks any caller that depends on the return value, as they will always receive nil when called from background threads. The function's contract promises to return the work result but fails to do so in the async dispatch path.

issues.title: MainThreadThrottler timing logic inverted causing throttling to never execute
issues.description: In the throttle method, lastExecutionTime is updated to Date() BEFORE checking the threshold guard condition. This means timeIntervalSinceNow will always be approximately 0 (since it was just set), which will never be less than -threshold (a negative value). The guard condition will always fail, preventing the completion from ever executing. This completely breaks the throttling mechanism, causing any code depending on throttled callbacks to never receive them.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31547 - Refactor FXIOS-13122 [Swift 6] Remove @Sendable from closures marked as @MainActor

structured_output.summary:
The PR removes redundant `@Sendable` annotations from closure types that are already `@MainActor` (a valid Swift 6 simplification) across about 40 files in BrowserKit and the app, tests, and extensions. It also contains three changes that are not part of that mechanical cleanup: a reordering inside `MainThreadThrottler.throttle`, removal of the main-thread hop in `handleServerTrust`, and a signature change that makes the generic `ensureMainThread<T>` return `T?`. Plus `final` is dropped from `WebServer` and a formatting nit lands in `RelayController`.

The mechanical part is correct. The non-mechanical parts introduce real defects. The throttler change makes the guard always fail (so throttled work never runs with the default 0.35s delay), and the existing `MainThreadThrottlerTests` would fail on it. The server-trust change calls a `@MainActor` completion handler from a background dispatch queue. I would not merge this as-is.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The throttler reorder is a logic regression that silently disables throttled UI work whenever a non-zero threshold is used, and the existing unit tests catch it. The server-trust change breaks main-thread confinement of a UI-isolated completion handler. Both need fixing before merge. The `@Sendable` removals themselves are fine.

architecture.overview:
Almost every changed site is a closure type alias or parameter annotated `@MainActor @Sendable`. Under Swift 6, a `@MainActor` closure is already implicitly `Sendable`, so the extra annotation is redundant. The PR strips it throughout the codebase, which is the intended change. The main-thread helpers `ensureMainThread` (in BrowserKit Common) and `MainThreadThrottler` (in the app) are the mechanism that bridges background callers, such as `DispatchQueue.main`, `dispatchQueue.async`, and GCDWebServer callbacks, onto the main actor.

The PR also changes behavior in three spots beyond the annotation cleanup: the debounce logic in `MainThreadThrottler.throttle`, the `handleServerTrust` callback path in `BrowserViewController`, and the return type of the generic `ensureMainThread<T>` overload. Those are where the review concentrates.
steps: Entry point: callers such as HomepageViewController and StoriesFeedViewController call `MainThreadThrottler.throttle(completion:)`, which debounces work and hops to `DispatchQueue.main`.

Change 1 (throttler): the PR moves `lastExecutionTime = Date()` above the guard. The guard then compares the freshly assigned timestamp to itself, so it always fails when threshold > 0, and the completion never runs.

Change 2 (server trust): `handleServerTrust` runs its check inside `dispatchQueue.async` (a background queue). The PR removes the `ensureMainThread` wrapper on the early-return branch, so the `@MainActor` completion handler now runs on a background thread. The accept branch still hops to main.

Change 3 (helper): the generic `ensureMainThread<T>` now returns `T?`, returning the value on the main thread and `nil` off it. Existing `Void`-closure callers are unaffected, but non-Void closures now produce unused-result results and get nil nondeterministically.

Mechanical change: `@Sendable` is removed from ~35 `@MainActor` closure types (MenuElement, Reducer, SingleActionViewModel, WKEngineWebView, the BVC delegate methods, and others). This is safe and matches the PR title.

diagrams.description: Shows how work from background callers reaches @MainActor closures, and where the PR changes the path.

findings.title: MainThreadThrottler never fires: timestamp is set before the guard
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Utils/MainThreadThrottler.swift`, `throttle(completion:)` (lines 25-28) assigns `lastExecutionTime = Date()` before the `guard` that compares `lastExecutionTime.timeIntervalSinceNow` against `-threshold`. That makes the guard always fail for positive thresholds, so the completion never runs. Restore the original order: keep the guard first, then assign `lastExecutionTime = Date()`, then dispatch. Confirm `MainThreadThrottlerTests` passes afterward.

findings.title: Completion handler invoked off the main thread in handleServerTrust
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/BrowserViewController/Extensions/BrowserViewController+WebViewDelegates.swift`, `handleServerTrust` (around lines 1340-1346) now calls the `@MainActor` `completionHandler(.performDefaultHandling, nil)` directly inside `dispatchQueue.async`, which runs on a background queue. Wrap that call back in `ensureMainThread { ... }` as it was before this PR, so it matches the accept branch a few lines below. Keep the rest of the function unchanged.

findings.title: Generic ensureMainThread<T> changed to return T? with silent nil off main
findings.body:
The PR changes `ensureMainThread<T>(execute:)` from returning `Void` to returning `T?`. This is unrelated to removing `@Sendable`, and the new contract is a trap. On the main thread the value comes back. Off the main thread the work is dispatched asynchronously and `nil` is returned, even when `T` is non-optional. Callers can't tell which case they're in.

Callers that pass a closure returning a non-Void value will now get an unused-result warning, which could break a `-warnings-as-errors` build. The `Void` overload still exists, so this is not needed for the stated refactor.

::diff{file="BrowserKit/Sources/Common/Utilities/DispatchQueueHelper.swift" lines="22-33"}

Revert the generic overload to its original `Void` form. If a value-returning helper is genuinely needed, make it `async` and use `MainActor.run` instead of returning `nil` off main.
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Sources/Common/Utilities/DispatchQueueHelper.swift`, the generic `ensureMainThread<T>(execute:)` (lines 22-33) was changed to return `T?`, returning `nil` off the main thread. This change is outside the PR's stated scope and makes callers get nondeterministic `nil` values. Revert this overload to its original `Void`-returning form. If a value-returning API is needed, implement it as an `async` function using `MainActor.run`. Verify that existing callers still compile without unused-result warnings.

findings.title: WebServer class loses `final` without explanation
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Application/WebServer.swift` line 18, `final` was removed from `class WebServer: WebServerProtocol, @unchecked Sendable`. This PR is about removing `@Sendable` and the `final` change is unrelated. Restore `final class WebServer`, unless a subclass is intended, in which case note it in the PR description.

findings.title: Double space in RelayPopulateCompletion typealias
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/RelayController.swift` line 10, the `RelayPopulateCompletion` typealias has a double space between `@MainActor` and `(`. Reduce it to a single space to match the rest of the codebase.

findings.title: Mechanical @Sendable removal on @MainActor closures is correct
findings.body:
Under Swift 6, a `@MainActor` function type is already `Sendable`, so `@MainActor @Sendable` is redundant, and dropping `@Sendable` is the right simplification. The change is applied consistently across the Redux `Reducer` typealias, `MenuElement`, `SingleActionViewModel`, `WKEngineWebView`, the BVC delegate methods, and the test mocks, so the signatures stay in sync. This is the bulk of the diff and I found no issues in it.
